passages.provision_quote: Sales of safe firearm storage devices.
passages.note: Bill text creates a TPT exemption for safe firearm storage devices, a tax-code change, not a rule on ownership, carry, or background checks.
House Third Reading roll call shows Gress voting Yes on HB2635, a single-subject tax-exemption bill for storage devices, not a firearm-regulation measure.
Bill Status page lists Gress as prime sponsor of HB2635, a TPT-exemption bill for firearm storage devices.

rows.reasoning: HB2635 (2025), which Gress prime-sponsored and voted Yes on, exempts "safe firearm storage devices" from transaction privilege tax; it does not speak to the ladder's rungs on banning ownership, banning assault-style weapons, requiring background checks, or carry-permit rules, so it is adjacent to the ladder's question "How should the government regulate firearms?" No source in the record addresses ownership, carry, or background-check regulation.
needs_source: Gress's own words or a legislative record on firearm ownership restrictions, assault-style weapon bans, universal background checks, or carry-permit rules (concealed/permitless carry)
